original_question:
Implement a Verilog module named `karnaugh_map`.
The module should have the following interface:
- Inputs: `wire A, B, C`
- Output: `reg F`

Inside the module, define four intermediate wires. These wires should represent the logical AND of input `A` with each of the four possible combinations of `B` and `C`. For example, one wire should represent `A & B & C`, another `A & B & ~C`, and so on.

Use an `always` block that is sensitive to changes in `A`, `B`, and `C`. Within this block, use a `case` statement based on the concatenated input `{A, B, C}` to assign a value to the output `F`. The assignment should select the value of one of the intermediate wires you defined, based on the following mapping:

- When the input `{A, B, C}` is `3'b000`, assign `F` the value of the wire representing `A & ~B & ~C`.
- When the input `{A, B, C}` is `3'b001`, assign `F` the value of the wire representing `A & ~B & C`.
- When the input `{A, B, C}` is `3'b010`, assign `F` the value of the wire representing `A & B & ~C`.
- When the input `{A, B, C}` is `3'b011`, assign `F` the value of the wire representing `A & B & C`.
- For input values `3'b100` through `3'b111`, the mapping pattern should be the same as for `3'b000` through `3'b011` respectively.

You may name the intermediate wires as you see fit, but the module name and the input/output names must match the specification.
